title: Residency orchestrator: evacuation scheduling, retention epochs & evidence sanitization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private require deterministic, auditable behavior when a region or VPC becomes unavailable. Current controls allow pinning nodes per-zone but lack a coordinated orchestration path that enforces tenant-specific retention epochs, produces tamper-evident evidence bundles for residency proofs, and sanitizes or quarantines ephemeral caches during forced cross-region evacuations. This ticket implements a policy-driven Residency Orchestrator that coordinates: (1) evacuation scheduling with maintenance and forced windows, (2) per-tenant retention epochs that apply to storage and transient KV caches, and (3) deterministic evidence bundle generation with optional redaction/sanitization rules for PII before export.
acceptance_criteria: API: Residency Orchestrator accepts a tenant-level policy object (pin, allowed_regions, retention_epoch_days, evacuation_window) and returns a validated plan
Retention: Storage retention enforcement applies per-tenant and retention_epoch updates trigger immutable audit events recorded in audit-log-store with signed checkpoints
Evacuation: Orchestrator can schedule a cross-region evacuation with a configurable grace period and optional immediate quarantine; execution path must respect tenant pins and produce a runbook entry

Evidence: For every evacuation or retention-change event, system generates an 'evidence bundle' (signed JSON + IMS metadata + location attestations) which can be exported via the Console and contains sanitized copies per tenant redaction policy
Simulator: Dry-run simulator produces evacuation plan and a predicted cost/latency delta; simulator results must be reproducible and match live-run behavior within 10% in baseline tests
Observability: Console shows per-tenant residency state, last evidence bundle timestamp, and a rollback button for canary evacuations
Security: Evidence bundles are signed with customer KMS keys when available and stored in encrypted archival bucket with retention aligned to tenant policy
implementation_plan: Design: Finalize Residency Orchestrator API schema and lifecycle transitions (draft at https://confluence.redwood.example/display/RES/Residency+Orchestrator+Spec)
Schema: Add tenant policy DB schema and immutable event ledger entries (use existing audit-log-store format)
Runtime: Implement coordinator service (golang) that talks to node agents to trigger cache-quarantine, storage quiesce, and region detach
Evidence: Build evidence bundler service that collects attestations from agents, signs with customer KMS (or platform key), attaches hashes of storage snapshots
Retention: Enforcement hooks in object-storage and cache-ttl manager to apply retention_epoch changes atomically
Simulator: Implement 'dry-run' mode in coordinator and a deterministic planner used by both simulator and live-run
Console: UX for tenant admins to configure policies, run dry-runs, download evidence bundles, and review evacuation timelines
Testing: E2E tests in staging with multi-region topology and fault injection; compliance test harness to validate evidence contents
Rollout: Canary on 5% Dedicated clusters -> 25% -> 100% with guarded automatic rollback on evidence mismatches
risks_mitigation: Risk: Evidence bundle may leak PII if sanitization rules are incomplete. Mitigation: start with conservative-allowlist redaction, enforce manual security review and require customer opt-in for verbose bundles

Risk: Forced evacuations may violate tenant pinning. Mitigation: coordinator validates tenant pins and if conflict exists, moves tenant to quarantine lane and emits incident ticket for manual resolution
Risk: KMS unavailability prevents signing. Mitigation: support cached platform-signed checkpoint with strict short TTL and queue async re-signing when KMS returns
Risk: Live-run differs from simulator. Mitigation: incremental canary runs, runbook checks, and automated comparison runner that blocks rollout on >10% deviation
